title: chi2cdf
summary: Evaluate the chi-square cumulative distribution function.

gpu_support.notes: Resident floating inputs use the host reference path and restore the result to the first owning provider. Resident integer input follows the same fallback in RunMat mode.

description: `chi2cdf(x,nu)` evaluates the chi-square CDF at `x` for degrees of freedom `nu`. `chi2cdf(x,nu,"upper")` returns the complementary upper-tail probability.
behaviors: `x` and `nu` support scalar expansion and matching array shapes.
Typed-integer `x` and `nu` values from all eight classes are mode-gated RunMat extensions and must lie within the exact-integer binary64 range.
Single-precision inputs produce single-precision output; otherwise output is double precision.
`nu` must be positive; invalid parameters produce `NaN` outputs.
Negative `x` values return zero for the lower tail and one for the upper tail.
The computation uses regularized incomplete gamma functions.

faqs.question: Why use the upper-tail form?
faqs.answer: The upper-tail form computes the complementary incomplete-gamma value directly, which is more stable for extreme upper tails than `1 - chi2cdf(...)`.
